# About the Author {.unnumbered}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="32%"}
![](images/davi_moreira_photo.JPG){width="90%" fig-alt="Portrait of Davi Moreira"}
:::
::: {.column width="68%"}
**Davi Moreira** is a Clinical Assistant Professor in the Quantitative Methods
Department and Director of the Daniels Undergraduate Business Honors Program
at Purdue University's Mitch Daniels School of Business. His work centers on
applied data science — statistics, natural language processing, predictive
analytics, causal inference, and artificial intelligence — with roots in
Political Communication, Comparative Politics, and Text as Data.

- Website: [davi-moreira.github.io](https://davi-moreira.github.io/){target="_blank"}
- Email: [dcordeir@purdue.edu](mailto:dcordeir@purdue.edu)
:::
:::

Before Purdue, he was an Assistant Professor of Political Science at the
Federal University of Pernambuco (UFPE), in Brazil, and held visiting
positions at Emory University and at UC San Diego's School of Global Policy
and Strategy. His doctoral research received the 2017 prize for the best
Brazilian Ph.D. dissertation in Political Science and International
Relations. Outside the university, he has worked as a Monitoring & Evaluation
Specialist consultant for the World Bank in Brazil, Mozambique, Angola, and
the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

These days, most of his time at Purdue goes into what this book is made of:
teaching business undergraduates to reason with data, directing an honors
program built around original research, and designing courses — including the
one this book grew out of — that train students to use AI hard and verify
everything it hands them. He wrote EDR|AI for the students he teaches:
undergraduates who want to produce research they can defend, in a world where
AI can produce almost everything else. The book's one rule is also his own
working rule: AI is your arm and your research assistant, not your brain.
